states.name: empty
states.gap: A sets the stats numbers heaviest of anything in the frame: the '0' carries 98 dark px to B's 71 and '< 1 min' 232 to B's 187 at identical #4A4A4A and identical cap height (~35% more ink, semibold vs medium), so on an empty document the loudest mark on the whole 2880x1800 sheet is a counter reading zero. Its page is also #F7F7F7 against B's #F9F9F9 — two levels greyer, a fractionally dirtier sheet.
states.gapTheirs: B draws the caret through the first glyph: caret occupies cols 626-631 while the 'S' of 'Start writing…' starts at col 624, so 6 device px (3 logical) of blue sit on top of the letter and bisect it — at 100% the S reads as a broken character. A's caret ends at col 624 and the S begins at 625: flush, no collision. B also titles an unsaved document 'Untitled.md', inventing a file extension for a file that does not exist.
states.verdict: The two bars are the same bars — same 32/26 px heights, same #4A4A4A number over #8C8C8C label, same Library and View icons to the pixel — so this comes down to two mistakes, and only B makes them. Opening B's empty document, the very first thing your eye lands on is a caret slicing the S of the placeholder in half; that is the one pixel a writer stares at before typing and B got it wrong. And the title bar tells you the document is called 'Untitled.md' when you have never saved anything — three characters of technical noise in the one strip whose whole job is to say nothing. A's cost is a stats bar that shouts its zeros in semibold; B's cost is a broken glyph and a lie in the title, and I would rather mute a bar than fix a caret.

states.name: typing
states.gap: A's dimmed bar is the louder of the two at the exact moment it is meant to be at a third: 91,143 total ink units vs B's 80,057 over the identical 500x20 device-px window centred on the stats block (~14% more ink), and it sits on a 2-level darker ground (#F7F7F7 vs #F9F9F9) so its label grey #CECECE clears the page by only 41 levels against B's #CFCFCF at 42 — A buys its hierarchy with insistence, not with recession. Its ink also starts one device row higher (1763 vs 1764), leaving the run 1.5 CSS px above the bar's optical centre against B's 1.25.
states.gapTheirs: B has no weight step worth the name between a number and its label. Measured as ink per px inside each run: B's '961' 20.1 against 'characters' 10.8 (1.86x) and '188' 20.8 against 'words' 10.9 (1.91x); A's are 22.8 vs 10.5 (2.17x) and 23.7 vs 10.1 (2.35x). The colour step is identical in both (#B6->#CF vs #B5->#CE), so this is purely weight: B's 'bold' number is barely bolder than its label, and '188 words' reads as one flat grey phrase you must actually stop and parse instead of a figure you catch peripherally.
states.verdict: There is almost nothing between these: both have taken the title bar away completely with no residue above y=232, both draw a 1px full-bleed hairline at the same y=1748 at 3.6% of ground, both give the bar the same 26 CSS px, both centre the same three stats on the window at x=1440, neither leaks a scrollbar. So it comes down to whether the bar is still readable at a glance once it has been dimmed, and only A's is: A's number stands at 2.2-2.35x the ink of its label, B's at 1.86-1.91x, which is the difference between clocking '188' out of the corner of your eye and having to look at it. B's flatter bar is quieter by 14%, and it bought that quiet by making the one thing on the bar you actually want stop working.

states.gap: The 'TYPEFACE' section heading is set regular-weight at #BABABA on the #F2F2F2 menu ground — about 1.7:1 — which is lighter and thinner than B's own disabled rows at #8C8C8C, so the seven dead 'Show Preview / Style Check / Settings…' rows read louder than the label that organises the menu. A sets the identical heading bold at #8C8C8C (~3.0:1), same 7 CSS px cap height.
states.gapTheirs: The View menu's label column is ragged in two positions: 'Sentence/Paragraph/Typewriter/Duo/Quattro/Mono/Dark Mode/Statistics' all set their left ink edge at device x≈2537, while 'Enable Focus Mode', 'Hide Bars' and 'All Commands…' hang at x≈2515 — a ~22 device px / ~11 CSS px step, and 'Hide Bars'/'All Commands…' sit in the *same* section, between the same two rules, as the 'Dark Mode'/'Statistics' they fail to line up with. B holds all 23 labels on a single column at device x=80 (±1 px), tick in a reserved gutter, selected row included.
states.verdict: Both bars are the same bar — 26 px stats strip, 1-device-px #DFDFDF hairline at the same y, the same #4A number against #8C label — so the whole decision lives in the menu, and A loses it on the first glance: three of eleven rows, including the selected one, hang eleven pixels out of the label column, two of them shoulder-to-shoulder with rows that don't. That is not a font-stack artifact; it is a rag inside one menu, and once you see it you will see it every time you reach for Ctrl+D. B's menu is longer and carries more greyed dead rows, but every label lands on one line and every chord right-aligns to one column, which is what a menu is for. B's only real sin is a section heading so faint it is outranked by its own unavailable commands — a grey value you can change in a minute, against a layout bug A would have to rebuild the row to fix.

states.name: palette
states.gap: Palette search placeholder is #BABABA on the #F2F2F2 panel (~1.6:1 contrast) where B sets it at #8C8C8C (~3.0:1) — same field, but A's 'Search commands' is a ghost, and it is lighter than A's own WRITE/TEXT section headings (#8C8C8C), inverting the hierarchy so the label ranks above the thing you type into. A's rule under the search field is also 1 device px (0.5 logical) against B's 2 (1 logical) — half the weight of A's own 1-logical-px panel border.
states.gapTheirs: The 32px title bar reads 'Untitled.md' for the same 188-word / 961-character document A names 'sample.md' — the bar's sole content, and self-contradictory: an untitled buffer carrying a file extension. Every other element of that bar is a pixel match (title text #8C8C8C, identical Library toggle and View glyphs, no rule beneath in either), so B spends its 32px telling the writer nothing about which draft is open.
states.verdict: Put them side by side and the palettes are the same panel: identical x979–1919 box, 726px tall, 48px (24 logical) rows, the same #0A94D6 selected pill, the same 51px chord inset, the same #4A4A4A number over #8C8C8C label in the stats bar and the same #DFDFDF hairline at the same y. So it comes down to two defects, one each. A hides its search prompt at #BABABA — you open a field you can't read until you start typing, which costs you the half-second before your first keystroke. B hides which file you are in, and that costs you every time you come back to the window with three drafts on the go; a title bar that says 'Untitled.md' over a named document has failed at the only job it has.
